question: What is database materialized view?

A query whose result is stored on disk
A table living only for one session
A structure speeding up row lookups

answer_explanation: Materialized view stores query result physically for faster access, refreshed periodically.

question: What is database covering index?

An index holding all a query needs
The column uniquely identifying a row
A column pointing at another table

answer_explanation: Covering index includes all columns query needs, avoiding table lookup.

question: What is database composite index?

options.option_value: Index on single column
Index on multiple columns
Primary key
Unique index

answer_explanation: Composite index spans multiple columns for queries filtering on those columns.

question: What is database index selectivity?

options.option_value: How much space the index occupies
How many distinct values it holds
How quickly a query comes back
How much disk the table consumes

answer_explanation: High selectivity means many distinct values, making index more effective.

question: What is database query execution plan?

options.option_value: The statement text the caller sent
The steps chosen to answer the query
The layout of the columns in a table
The definition of a lookup structure

answer_explanation: Execution plan shows how database will execute query, helping optimization.

question: What is database full table scan?

Reading every row in table
Reading specific columns
Reading from cache

answer_explanation: Full table scan reads all rows when index cannot be used effectively.

question: What is database query optimizer?

The part choosing how to run a query
The part that builds lookup structures
The part that bulk loads rows in

answer_explanation: Query optimizer analyzes queries and chooses most efficient execution plan.

Handles opened and never given back
A missing structure over a column

answer_explanation: N+1 problem executes query for parent then N queries for children instead of join.

question: How to solve N+1 query problem?

options.option_value: Build more lookup structures
Fetch the related rows in one join
Split the rows across more machines
Serve repeat reads from memory

answer_explanation: Eager loading fetches related data in single query using JOINs.

question: What is database transaction isolation level?

options.option_value: How many transactions may run at once
How much concurrent transactions may see
How quickly a transaction completes
How many rows a transaction may touch

answer_explanation: Isolation levels control visibility of uncommitted changes between transactions.

question: What is read uncommitted isolation level?

options.option_value: The strictest level on offer
The loosest level, permitting dirty reads
The level preventing every anomaly
The level chosen by default everywhere

answer_explanation: Read uncommitted allows reading uncommitted changes (dirty reads).

question: What is read committed isolation level?

options.option_value: Allows dirty reads
Prevents dirty reads only
Prevents all anomalies
Serializable

answer_explanation: Read committed prevents dirty reads but allows non-repeatable reads.

question: What is repeatable read isolation level?

options.option_value: The level permitting non-repeatable reads
The level preventing dirty and repeat reads
The strictest level available on offer
The loosest level available on offer

answer_explanation: Repeatable read ensures same query returns same results during transaction.

question: What is serializable isolation level?

options.option_value: The loosest level available on offer
The strictest level, as if run in turn
The level preventing only dirty reads
The level preventing non-repeatable reads

answer_explanation: Serializable provides highest isolation, executing transactions as if serial.

question: What is phantom read?

New rows appearing on a repeated query
One row showing two different values
Seeing rows that have been removed

answer_explanation: Phantom read occurs when new rows appear in repeated query due to other transaction.

question: What is database write skew?

options.option_value: Reading a value that was never written
Two transactions deciding on stale reads
A single transaction failing to commit
A lookup structure that has gone bad

answer_explanation: Write skew: concurrent transactions read overlapping data and update inconsistently.

question: What is database MVCC?

Multi-version concurrency control
A minimum viable cache arrangement
A maximum volume control setting

answer_explanation: MVCC maintains multiple versions of data for concurrent access without locking.

question: What is database vacuum/analyze?

options.option_value: Statements the application runs itself
Housekeeping that keeps performance up
Taking periodic copies of the data
Checking who is allowed to read what

question: What is database table bloat?

A table wasting space after churn
A table holding a great many rows
A table holding a great many columns

answer_explanation: Table bloat occurs when updates/deletes leave unused space not reclaimed.

question: What is database hot standby?

A copy already answering read queries
The node that accepts all the writes
A store for frequently read values

answer_explanation: Hot standby is active read replica that can quickly become primary if needed.

question: What is database warm standby?

options.option_value: A copy already answering read queries
A copy running but serving nobody
The node that accepts all the writes
A file written out and left on disk

answer_explanation: Warm standby is running but not serving queries, faster recovery than cold backup.

question: What is database cold backup?

options.option_value: A copy kept continuously in step
A copy taken with the system stopped
A copy already answering read queries
A copy that lags the primary slightly

answer_explanation: Cold backup is offline copy of database, not actively running.

question: What is point-in-time recovery?

Restoring to any chosen moment in time
Keeping a copy continuously in step
Switching to a standby automatically

answer_explanation: PITR restores database to specific point using base backup and WAL logs.

Recording the change before applying it
Writing the change into a memory cache
Writing the change without waiting

Flushing logged changes into data files
The moment a query begins executing
The moment a lookup structure is built

answer_explanation: Checkpoint writes dirty buffers and WAL records to permanent storage.

question: What is database replication lag?

How long a single query takes to run
How long a packet takes to cross

answer_explanation: Replication lag is time delay for changes to reach replica from primary.

question: What is synchronous replication?

The primary waits for the copy to confirm
No copying takes place at any point
Copying is deliberately held back a while

answer_explanation: Synchronous replication waits for replica to confirm before committing.

question: What is asynchronous replication?

options.option_value: The primary waits for the copy to confirm
The primary commits without waiting
No copying takes place at any point
Copying happens only during maintenance

answer_explanation: Asynchronous replication commits on primary without waiting for replica.

An automatic switch after a failure
Taking a periodic copy of the data
Sending each query to the right node

A deliberate switch made on purpose
Restoring a copy taken earlier
Configuring copies for the first time

answer_explanation: Switchover is planned manual transition from primary to standby.

A separate deployment per customer

A separate store for each customer
A separate schema inside one store
